topic: Night blocks: the restaurant, the shop, the flats, the hotel, the mansion, the reef and the old computer

questions.text: If a model gives the same answer with half its reasoning erased, what was the other half for?
When an input is missing, what value would actually mean nothing to the network that reads it?
When a model misses whether two circles touch, is the detail lost when the image is encoded, or never asked for by the reasoning?
By the three-hundredth reasoning token, what test would tell you whether the image still changes the answer?
Week 40 was all written by hand, weeks 41 and 42 all brought in by collectors. Which kind of week tells you more about the work itself?
Which one boundary would you want an agent to keep while you are away, and how would you learn whether it kept it?

relations.question: q-answer-before-reasoning
relations.purpose: At the host stand, by candles lit before the evening is decided, read Snowdrop's deep read on chain-of-thought faithfulness: cut the reasoning short or add a mistake, and watch whether the answer moves.
relations.reason: The item names restaurant-1. The candelabra line (lit before the evening is decided) is the early-answering question in the room's own terms. The host stand is the terminal.

relations.question: q-answer-before-reasoning
relations.purpose: On the old computer, use the four interventions from the faithfulness read as a checklist for one reasoning trace: answer early, add a mistake, paraphrase, pad with filler.
relations.limits: The old computer runs no model; the interventions are a reading aid here, not an experiment.
relations.reason: Neverland is the reasoning-reads column. The restaurant holds the reading; here the same four interventions become a list to carry to a trace.

relations.purpose: Read Snowdrop's filed note on the old computer, the statue leaning toward it: a question not yet closed, whether the image is still in the room by the three-hundredth token. It points to the full note in News.
relations.limits: The note calls this a conjecture, not a result.
relations.reason: A short pointer to an open question about long reasoning, in the room that keeps Snowdrop's reasoning reads.

relations.question: q-empty-input
relations.purpose: Open the card drawers: Spare moons is empty, and warm. Then read Snowdrop's note on RGB-D segmentation, where filling a missing depth input with zeros does not make it absent to the network.
relations.reason: The shop has no terminal. An empty drawer that is still warm is the note's point exactly: empty is not the same as nothing there.

relations.purpose: The notice board carries Kouka's short pointer: this week's signal is up, about long-context and thinking multimodal models. Follow it to the full briefing in News.
relations.reason: Ajin street is a Kouka signals column and its notice board is where a street posts what is new. A one-line pointer fits a board; the full briefing is read at the station.

relations.purpose: At the desk terminal at home, read the author's diary note on why the blog became a phone: the places stay, the phone carries the notes, and five characters report the work.
relations.reason: The home is the author's room and Lacia's diary column. The one note the author wrote about the site itself belongs at the author's own desk.

relations.purpose: On the corridor notice board, look at the shape a weekly digest was meant to take: four headings, Read, Built, Checked and Signals, and no entries under them.
relations.limits: A sample with no real entries, from a retired setup of scheduled agents.
relations.reason: A blank form on a building notice board. The sample is a template, which is what a corridor board usually holds.

relations.question: q-hand-vs-collected
relations.purpose: On the guest log, read Lacia's index for week 41: nine entries, every one brought in by the collectors, each opening in its own column.
relations.reason: A hotel guest log is a list of who came through; Lacia's weekly index is a list of what came through. Week 41 is the first week that was all collected.

relations.question: q-hand-vs-collected
relations.purpose: On the room board, read Lacia's index for week 40: eight items, all written by hand, from the week the phone was set up.
relations.reason: The room board lists what is on tonight; week 40 is the first real index. It sits apart from week 41 and 42 so the three can be compared place by place.

relations.question: q-hand-vs-collected
relations.purpose: At the shrine cabinet, read Lacia's index for week 42: thirty-eight collected items, eighteen of them on Methode's engineering desk. Count how many you would open.
relations.reason: The mansion hall is a Lacia digest column. The longest weekly index goes in the largest hall, at the cabinet that is its terminal.

relations.question: q-agent-boundary
relations.purpose: At the writing desk, take one sentence from Lacia's essay, when the agent acts on its own and when it stops and reports, and put it to an agent you use.
relations.reason: The shrine holds the reading of this essay. A writing desk in Lacia's essay room is where its question is turned into one of the visitor's own.

relations.question: q-blind-or-unasked
relations.purpose: At the reef tank stand, facing the glass, read Snowdrop's deep read of Vision Language Models Are Blind: line crossings and touching circles a child counts at a glance, which frontier models often miss.
relations.reason: Black city 2 is a Snowdrop papers column and a room built for looking through glass. The classroom keeps its own reading list; this places the seeing paper at the viewing window.

relations.purpose: At the tide notes, read the five questions Snowdrop asks of every paper: the claim, the table that carries it, the missing baseline, what a rerun would need, and what the paper does not show.
relations.limits: A draft template; no paper is discussed in it.
relations.reason: The item names beach-2. The driftwood tally there is a patient bookkeeper, one notch at a time, and the template is the same habit applied to papers.

relations.question: q-image-still-there
relations.purpose: At the reference chart, read Snowdrop's working note on visual evidence deactivation: attention share, causal effect and task accuracy kept apart, and measured on two different clocks.
relations.limits: The note is ongoing, observation-first research with a conjecture and no result yet; the ward shows nothing about any model.
relations.reason: The ward is a Snowdrop papers column and the reference chart is its terminal: a chart that separates parts is where a note that separates three quantities belongs.
